outline:
本課程旨在探討如何將 AI 技術應用於語用學研究，著重多元社會情境與語境之下之語言使用分析與詮釋。此課程將深入淺出討論語用學核心理論部分，並結合 AI 大型語言模型 (例如: GPT, Gemini, 以及 Claude 等) 實際操作，讓學生親自學習辨識、分析與評估各種自然語言表現，包含言語行為 (speech acts)、會話隱含 (conversational implicature) 及禮貌策略 (politeness strategies) 等現象。本課程以專題式學習融合理論與實務, 幫助同學從全新的 AI 驅動視角進行語用學研究, 在分析人類真實語言互動行為之外, 更同時能了解 AI 生成文本在語用能力方面的優勢與局限。
AI & Pragmatics is a graduate-level course that explores how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the study of pragmatics by focusing on the analysis and interpretation of language use across diverse social and contextual settings. Students will integrate core theories of pragmatics with hands-on experience using Large Language Models (e.g., GPT, Gemini, and Claude) to identify, analyze, and evaluate key pragmatic phenomena such as speech acts, conversational implicatures, and politeness strategies—and, more importantly, apply these skills to real-world language tasks. Built around project-based learning, the course blends theory with practice, preparing students to conduct research in pragmatics from a fresh, AI-driven perspective. It equips them not only to analyze authentic language interactions but also to critically assess the strengths and limitations of AI-generated texts in terms of pragmatic competence.
schedule:
UNITE 1: Foundations of Pragmatics
Weeks 1–6: Understanding Key Pragmatic Concepts

W1 Introduction to Pragmatics
● What is pragmatics?
● Pragmatics vs. semantics vs. syntax
● The role of context in meaning

W2 Speech Act Theory (Austin & Searle)
● Locution, illocution, perlocution
● Different types of speech acts
● Hands-on: Identifying speech acts in dialogues

W3 Conversational Implicature and Grice's Maxims
● Cooperative Principle (CP) and Gricean Maxims
● How do implicatures create indirect meaning?
● Heads-on: Finding implicatures in real conversations

W4 Politeness Strategies & Face Theory
● Brown & Levinson's politeness theory
● Cultural variation in politeness
● Hands-on: Analyzing politeness strategies in dialogues

W5 Conversational Structure & Discourse Coherence
● Turn-taking, adjacency pairs, and repairs
● What makes discourse coherent? (pragmatic/discourse markers)
● Hands-on: Identifying coherence markers in texts

W6 Pragmatic Failures & Miscommunication
● When pragmatics go wrong: misunderstanding, humor, sarcasm
● Case studies of misinterpretation
● Hands-on: Analyzing pragmatic failure in conversations

W7 Holiday (No Class)

W8 Review Session—Bridging Pragmatics & AI
(Review of Key Pragmatic Concepts Before the Midterm)
● Recap of speech acts, implicature, politeness, discourse coherence
● How is pragmatics challenging for AI and NLP models?
● Introduction to AI-based tools for pragmatics
● Hands-on: Exploring AI-generated dialogue for pragmatic features

W9 Midterm Exam

UNIT 2: AI and NLP for Pragmatic Analysis
Weeks 10–14: Applying AI and NLP to Pragmatics

W10 Introduction to AI and NLP for Pragmatics
● Overview of AI in linguistics & pragmatics
● How do AI models process pragmatic meaning?
● Hands-on: Exploring AI-generated conversations

W11 AI and Speech Act Recognition
● Can AI detect speech acts?
● NLP models for speech act classification
● Hands-on: Using AI to classify speech acts in dialogues

W12 AI and Conversational Implicature Detection
● Can AL infer meaning beyond the literal?
● Case study: AI-generated implicatures vs, human interpretation
● Hands-on: Testing AI's ability to interpret implicatures

W13 AI and Politeness Analysis
● How do AI evaluate politeness in conversations?
● Bias in AI-generated politeness
● Hands-on: Using AI to analyze politeness in different contexts

W14 AI and Discourse Coherence–Can AI maintain Context
● How do AI models track coherence across discourse?
● Case study: Chatbot failures in maintaining coherent conversations
● Hands-on: Evaluating AI's discourse coherence

UNIT 3: AI, Bias, and Pragmatic Challenges
Weeks 15–16: Ethical and Applied Perspectives

W15 AI Bias in Pragmatics–"Who Gets to Be Polite?"
● How does AI encode social & cultural biases in pragmatics?
● Examples of AI misinterpreting pragmatic meaning
● Hands-on: Analyzing bias in AI-generated dialogue.

W16 AI-Assisted Pragmatic Research–Practical Applications
● How can researchers use AI to study pragmatic patterns?
● Workshop: Designing an AI-assisted pragmatic study.

W17 Final Presentations & Course Wrap-Up
● Students present their AI-assisted pragmatic research projects.
● Course reflection & feedback

W18 Final Project Due

materials:
Class readings will be selected from, but not limited to, the following references.
----------------------------------------

Ariel, M. (2010). Defining pragmatics. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

Brown, P., & Levinson, S. C. (1987). Politeness: Some universals in language use. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. (Original work published 1978)

Grice, H. P. (1975). Logic and Conversation. In P. Cole, & J. L. Morgan. (Eds.), Syntax and Semantics, Vol. 3, Speech Acts (pp. 41–58). New York: Academic Press.

Horn, L. R., & Ward, G. (2006). (Eds.). The handbook of pragmatics. Oxford: Blackwell.

Kecskes, I. (2014). Intercultural pragmatics. Oxford: Oxford University Press.

Levinson, S. C. (1983). Pragmatics. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

Sperber, D., & Wilson, D. (1995). Relevance: Communication and cognition. Oxford: Blackwell. (Original work published 1986)

---The course will be taught in English, while students can choose to examine different natural languages for their final projects.
